issues.description: The problem statement (UML) specifies getTotalNumberOfStudents() should return an int, but the provided solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning a StudentCount object (a custom wrapper). This is a structural return-type mismatch that can confuse students: the UML and task text guide them to implement an int-returning method, while the solution demonstrates a different API requiring an extra class.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Change the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (summing inscribed and guest students) to match the UML and problem text and remove or make StudentCount optional; or (B) Update the problem statement and UML to specify that getTotalNumberOfStudents() returns a StudentCount and document the StudentCount class in the template so students know to use it. Ensure the template Lecture.java signature and any tests match the chosen approach.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) specifies getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int (a primitive integer total), but the solution introduces a new StudentCount class and implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return StudentCount. This introduces a new identifier (StudentCount) for the concept 'total number of students' and changes the return type compared to the UML and the template expectations, creating a mapping/confusion for students who expect a simple int total.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the representation of the total number of students consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (sum of inscribed and guest students) and remove the StudentCount wrapper class, matching the UML/problem statement; or (B) update the problem statement and UML to document the StudentCount type (and its purpose) so students expect a wrapper class instead of a primitive. Prefer option A for minimal cognitive overhead.
